_about: The FAQ for meringominutes.app. tools/sync.py writes /faq/ (the <details> list and its FAQPage JSON-LD) from this file, and assets/js/ask-ui.js answers from it in the browser. Answers are plain text; a link is written [text](/path/). Every number in an answer is listed, in reading order, in `facts` by its data/facts.json id; `app` lists quotations of the app's own words. The assistant indexes q, alt and keywords only, never the answer.
disclosure: Automated answers from this site's FAQ — not a person.
refusal: I found nothing on this site that says that.
_gate: An answer needs all three: score >= minScore, coverage >= minCoverage (the share of the question's meaningful words that matched the entry) and best/runner-up >= minMargin. minCoverage is 0.6 rather than 0.5 so that one matched word out of two is not enough: at 0.5, "How do I cancel my subscription" and "Can I pay with PayPal?" get a price answer. minScore is a floor set just under the lowest correct answer in tests/faq-eval.json (4.8); on this corpus scores do not separate in-scope from out-of-scope questions, coverage does.

entries.q: Does it work offline?
alt: Can I use it without internet?
entries.answer: Yes, once the models are downloaded. By default, recording, transcription and the summary all run on your Mac. The internet is needed only to download each model the first time.
sources: COPY-BLOCKS: FAQ, offline; privacy panel green
claims.csv: The only non-localhost endpoints the app itself contacts are model downloads

entries.q: Is my data encrypted?
alt: Are my recordings protected on disk?
entries.answer: No, and I'd rather say so plainly. Recordings and meeting files are ordinary files in a folder in your Library, and the app adds no encryption of its own. macOS file permissions protect them, and FileVault does too if it's on. By default nothing is uploaded, so there's no server copy to protect.
sources: claims.csv: Nothing is encrypted at rest; COPY-BLOCKS: FAQ, encrypted; S2 §1c

entries.q: Does anything about my meetings get sent anywhere?
alt: Does it collect analytics or crash reports?
entries.answer: By default, no. The only traffic is models coming in the first time they're needed, and there's no analytics, telemetry or crash-reporting code in the app. If you point the summariser at Ollama on another machine, each transcript goes there, and the privacy panel turns orange and names it.
sources: claims.csv: The only non-localhost endpoints the app itself contacts are model downloads; No analytics, telemetry or crash-reporting SDK is present; COPY-BLOCKS: privacy panel green
claims.csv: The app warns, in orange and by name; COPY-BLOCKS: privacy panel orange

entries.q: Does it check for updates?
entries.answer: Not in the current build, which never contacts an update server. When I add an update check, the privacy page will say what it sends, in the same release.
sources: claims.csv: The shipped build never contacts an update server

entries.q: Where are my recordings kept?
entries.answer: In ~/Library/Application Support/Meringo Minutes/, one folder for everything. Deleting a meeting moves it to the Trash, so you can get it back until you empty it.

entries.q: Does it need Screen Recording permission?
alt: How does it hear the other side of a call?
Why would it want screen recording?
entries.answer: No. It hears the other side of a call through a Core Audio tap, so it never asks for Screen Recording.
sources: claims.csv: System audio is captured via a Core Audio process tap

entries.q: Can I run the summariser on another computer?
alt: Can I use a remote Ollama server?
Can I use a more powerful machine on my network?
entries.answer: Yes: point the server URL in Settings at another machine running Ollama. Each transcript is then sent there, and the privacy panel turns orange and names the machine. The audio and the transcript stay stored on your Mac.
sources: COPY-BLOCKS: privacy panel orange; claims.csv: The app warns, in orange and by name

entries.q: What does it read on my Mac?
alt: What permissions does it ask for?
entries.answer: Your microphone, the audio your Mac plays during a call, and your calendar, to name meetings. Reminders when you send a commitment there, and your own Contacts card only when you ask. The signature holds exactly three entitlements: audio input, address book and calendars.
sources: S2 §1c: permissions; app CHANGELOG 1.1.0: Recording and transcription
claims.csv: The app requests exactly three entitlements

entries.q: Does this website track me?
entries.answer: No cookies and no analytics. It keeps your theme choice in your browser. GitHub, which hosts the site, logs IP addresses for security. [The privacy page](/privacy/) has the details.

entries.q: How accurate is the transcription?
alt: How many words does it get wrong?
entries.answer: It gets about one word in five wrong: an 18.4% median word error rate across 66 bench recordings. In the demo it heard “locum” as “locker” and “agreed” as “gag read”.
sources: claims.csv: 18.4 % median WER on 66 bench recordings

entries.q: Can I trust the summary?
entries.answer: As far as you can check it. Most summary sentences carry a timestamp, and with Ollama a second model sets aside what it can't support. Neither is perfect. In the demo, 4 of 11 timestamps point at a line that doesn't state the claim, and the check kept a sentence that merged two facts.

entries.q: Do the timestamps point to the right place?
alt: Why doesn't the first paragraph have a timestamp?
entries.answer: Near it. In the demo, none of the 11 landed on a line that states the whole claim: 4 point at a line that doesn't state it, and the other 7 at a line that states only part of it. The 4 misses land early, and the supporting line follows within about 30 seconds. The overview at the top never gets a timestamp, by design, and a sentence the app can't place gets none rather than a guess.

entries.q: How well does it tell speakers apart?
alt: Does it know who said what?
Does it get speakers mixed up?
Does it recognise my voice across meetings?
entries.answer: It found all three voices in the demo and gave 5 of the 56 lines to the wrong one. No voice is stored or matched from one meeting to the next, so you name the voices once per meeting.
sources: claims.csv: No voice is stored or matched across meetings; capture README §5

entries.q: How long does it take to process a meeting?
alt: How long until my notes are ready?
Can it handle a two-hour meeting?
entries.answer: One meeting has been timed on the current build: 3 minutes 53 seconds of audio took about 6½ to 7 minutes, on an M4 with 24 GB, with the speech models already downloaded. The app sets no length limit, but I haven't timed a long meeting on this build, so I won't give you a per-hour figure yet.

entries.q: Does it find action items?
alt: Does it list who committed to what?
entries.answer: Yes. Each one has an owner, and it gets a date only when the meeting gave one certain day. It's the part I'd check hardest. In the demo it listed 8 items for 5 commitments, with Dana's locum task in three wordings.

entries.q: What is Ask?
alt: Can I ask questions about a meeting?
Can I search a meeting by asking?
entries.answer: A tab where you put a question to a meeting in plain words. Each sentence of the answer comes with the transcript lines it cites. You can ask one meeting, or all of them at once.
sources: ASK-BANK: How to read this; app CHANGELOG 1.1.0: Ask

entries.q: What happens when the meeting doesn't answer my question?
alt: What if the answer isn't in the meeting?
entries.answer: It says “I found nothing in this meeting that says that.” and stops there. In the demo it did that for all 8 questions the meeting doesn't answer, or answers only in part, including one where a plausible day rate was one division away.
app: I found nothing in this meeting that says that.

entries.q: Does Ask ever get it wrong?
alt: Does Ask refuse things it shouldn't?
entries.answer: Yes. In the demo it refused one question the meeting did answer, and it added “dollars” to another answer when nobody named a currency. Asked again, it gave the same answer word for word, mistake included.

entries.q: What does “Checked” mean?
alt: What does the Checked label mean?
entries.answer: A second, different model has read the summary against the transcript and moved what it couldn't support into a separate card. This build shows one Checked mark for the whole summary. It doesn't mark sentences one by one.
sources: AUDIT: What "the app's own state" means; DECISIONS 2026-09-21

entries.q: What's the difference between traced and checked?
alt: Is a timestamp the same as a check?
entries.answer: Traced means a sentence carries a timestamp, placed by plain code with no model involved, on every setup. Checked means a second model read the summary and set aside what it couldn't support, and that needs Ollama. A timestamp can still point at the wrong line, and a checked summary can still hold a mistake.

entries.q: Will the check find all the mistakes?
alt: Can a wrong sentence get past the check?
entries.answer: No. In the demo it kept a sentence that merged two facts, and it passed an Ask answer that added “dollars”. It also sets aside sentences that are nearly right. It catches some mistakes, and reading the transcript catches more.

entries.q: What happens to the sentences it sets aside?
alt: What is the unverified sentences card?
entries.answer: They go in a folded card under the summary, headed with a count, such as “4 unverified sentences”. The card's own line is “Read it as a lead, not a finding.” In this build they carry no timestamp.
app: Read it as a lead, not a finding.
sources: AUDIT: What "the app's own state" means

entries.q: Why does my summary say Not checked?
alt: What if the summary wasn't checked?
entries.answer: It tells you why: the check model isn't downloaded, Ollama wasn't running, the check is off, or it stopped part-way. Check Now checks the summary without writing it again.
sources: app CHANGELOG 1.1.0: audit-t1; capture README §6, frame 03

entries.q: What do I need to run it?
alt: Will it run on my Mac?
entries.answer: A Mac with Apple Silicon, running macOS 27 or later, plus Ollama. Ollama is a free app, and the setup assistant finds it or installs it for you. Older versions of macOS won't run it, and I haven't settled whether they ever could.
sources: claims.csv: Apple Silicon only; Requires macOS 27.0; app README: Getting started

entries.q: Does it run on an Intel Mac?
alt: Will it work on an older MacBook?
entries.answer: No. It's built for Apple Silicon only.

entries.q: Is there a Windows, iPhone or iPad version?
alt: Can I record on my phone?
entries.answer: No. Meringo Minutes runs on the Mac only.
sources: claims.csv: Requires macOS 27.0; Apple Silicon only

entries.q: How much does it download?
alt: How much disk space does it need?
entries.answer: The app is 84 MB, with no models inside it. The default setup adds about 710 MB of speech models, Ollama, and two language models of 9.0 GB and 4.7 GB, so plan on about 15 GB of disk.
sources: SITE-FACTS-2026-09-23; claims.csv: No model weights are bundled

entries.q: How much memory does it need?
alt: Will it run on 8 GB or 16 GB?
entries.answer: I don't know the minimum yet. I've measured it only on an M4 with 24 GB.

entries.q: What is Ollama, and why do I need it?
alt: Can I use it without Ollama?
entries.answer: Ollama is a free app that runs language models, by default on your own Mac. Meringo Minutes uses it for the summary, the check and Ask. Without it, a meeting is still transcribed and its summary waits for Ollama. Apple Intelligence is listed in Settings as experimental.
sources: app README: Getting started; SYNTH addendum; DECISIONS 2026-09-21

entries.q: Can I import a recording I already have?
alt: Can I summarise an audio file?
Does it work on old recordings?
entries.answer: Yes. Import Audio takes a file, and the demo on this site was made that way. It accepts m4a, wav, mp3, aiff and mp4.

entries.q: How much does it cost?
entries.answer: $79 during the first month after launch, then $99. You pay once, and there's no subscription.

entries.q: When can I buy it?
entries.answer: Not yet, and I don't have a date to give you. Email support@meringo.app and I'll send one note when it's ready.

entries.q: Is there a free trial?
entries.answer: One is planned, not built. The free version will process the first 30 minutes of each meeting, and buying processes the rest from the audio it already kept. There's no clock on it.

entries.q: Is it on the Mac App Store?
alt: Can I get it from the App Store?
entries.answer: No. It'll be sold directly, through a link on this site.
sources: S2 §1a; claims.csv: docs/SELLING.md rules the Mac App Store out for this build

entries.q: Is it open source?
alt: Can I see the source code?
entries.answer: No.

entries.q: Will the other people in the meeting know?
alt: Does it announce that it's recording?
Is the recording obvious to others?
entries.answer: Yes, by default. As recording starts, the app says out loud: “I'm recording this meeting to take notes. The recording stays on my Mac.” You can change the words or switch it off, and it stays on until you do. A recording made without it is marked Unannounced.
app: I'm recording this meeting to take notes. The recording stays on my Mac.
sources: COPY-BLOCKS: what the app says out loud
COPY-BLOCKS: FAQ, other people; app CHANGELOG 1.1.0: Recording and transcription

entries.q: Does it join my calls as a bot?
alt: Does it add a bot to Zoom?
Does it send a calendar invite?
entries.answer: No. Nothing joins the call and no calendar invite goes out; it records the call's audio on your Mac. That's why the announcement is on by default: it's how the others find out.
sources: COPY-BLOCKS: FAQ, other people; claims.csv: Core Audio process tap

entries.q: Does it know which recording law applies to me?
alt: Is it legal to record my meeting?
Does it handle one-party and two-party consent?
entries.answer: No, and it doesn't try. The reason is in the code: “the strictest participant's law governs, and nobody's location is knowable.” That's a design choice, not legal advice. One more limit: on headphones, the far end of a call may not hear the announcement.

entries.q: Can it start recording by itself?
alt: Does it record automatically when a call starts?
entries.answer: Only if you turn that on. It's off by default, it works only while announcements are on, and it announces before it records.

entries.q: What languages does it understand?
alt: Does it support French or German?
entries.answer: The default speech model lists English and 24 other European languages, and Whisper, in Settings, lists 99. I've measured accuracy in English only: every recording in my benchmark is English, so I can't tell you how it does in the others. The vocabulary list works in English only.

entries.q: What can I export?
alt: Can I export to Markdown or PDF?
Can I get the transcript out?
entries.answer: The summary (with or without timestamps), the transcript and the mindmap, as Markdown, plain text, PDF, Mermaid or OPML, or everything to a folder at once. An exported summary says whether it was checked.

entries.q: Can I teach it names and jargon?
entries.answer: Yes. Add a word to the vocabulary list, and the app changes it wherever it also hears it in the audio. On three bench meetings full of uncommon names, read by synthesised voices, lists halved the error rate, from 10.9% to 5.4%. In the demo, “Pemberton” was fixed both times, and “locum”, heard as “locker”, stayed wrong.
sources: claims.csv: Vocabulary lists halved WER; S2 §1g

entries.q: Does it suggest corrections by itself?
entries.answer: Sometimes. When it notices a near-miss it offers the correction, and you confirm it. On the bench it made 14 offers, and all 14 were right. In the demo it made none.

entries.q: Does it work with Zoom, Teams or Google Meet?
alt: Which call apps does it support?
entries.answer: It records your microphone and the audio your Mac plays, so the call app doesn't matter. It doesn't connect to any of them.
sources: S2 §3: system-audio permission string; claims.csv: entitlements; Core Audio process tap

entries.q: Can I share meetings with my team?
entries.answer: No. There's no sync and no account. You can export a meeting and send it yourself.
sources: COPY-BLOCKS: privacy panel green; capture README §8

entries.q: Why pay for this if I only need a transcript?
entries.answer: If a transcript is all you need, you may not need Meringo Minutes. The price is for the parts that help you check the notes: the timestamps, the second model's check, and an Ask that says when the meeting doesn't answer.

entries.q: Who makes Meringo Minutes?
entries.answer: I do: Adam Siemaszko, under Meringo Labs LLC, in Erie County, New York. Write to me at support@meringo.app.
